blocks.en: A Word Before We Begin
blocks.es_reference: Una Palabra Antes de Comenzar

blocks.en: The Latter-day Saints present Mormonism as another branch of Christianity, and their missionaries carry the name of Jesus around the world. But the Jesus they carry is not the Jesus of the Bible, and their gospel is not the gospel of grace. Mormonism teaches a God who was once a man and a man who may become a god, a plurality of gods, and a salvation completed by our own works and temple rites. That is not a variation within the faith; it is another faith in Christian dress. And where the Bible gives us the eternal Son, Mormonism rests finally on the word of Joseph Smith, a man — for a later prophet, however sincere, cannot overturn the finished revelation of God. We weigh it by the Word of God and, where it departs from the gospel, say so plainly and in love (Ephesians 4:15).
blocks.es_reference: Los Santos de los Últimos Días presentan el mormonismo como otra rama del cristianismo, y sus misioneros llevan el nombre de Jesús por todo el mundo. Pero el Jesús que llevan no es el Jesús de la Biblia, y su evangelio no es el evangelio de la gracia. El mormonismo enseña un Dios que una vez fue hombre y un hombre que puede llegar a ser dios, una pluralidad de dioses, y una salvación completada por nuestras propias obras y ritos del templo. Eso no es una variación dentro de la fe; es otra fe vestida de cristiana. Y donde la Biblia nos da al Hijo eterno, el mormonismo descansa finalmente en la palabra de José Smith, un hombre — pues un profeta posterior, por sincero que sea, no puede derribar la revelación consumada de Dios. La pesamos por la Palabra de Dios y, donde se aparte del evangelio, lo decimos con claridad y con amor (Efesios 4:15).

blocks.en: Who Are the Latter-day Saints?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Quiénes Son los Santos de los Últimos Días?

blocks.en: The Latter-day Saints, members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, trace their beginning to Joseph Smith in the United States in the 1820s and 1830s. They teach that true Christianity fell into a "Great Apostasy" after the apostles and was restored through Joseph Smith. They are directed by a living prophet and apostles, use their own additional scriptures, build temples for sacred ordinances, and are widely known for their young missionaries. Much in their conduct is admirable. Our concern is not their diligence but what they teach about God, about Christ, and about salvation.
blocks.es_reference: Los Santos de los Últimos Días, miembros de La Iglesia de Jesucristo de los Santos de los Últimos Días, sitúan su comienzo en José Smith, en los Estados Unidos, en las décadas de 1820 y 1830. Enseñan que el cristianismo verdadero cayó en una "Gran Apostasía" después de los apóstoles y fue restaurado por medio de José Smith. Son dirigidos por un profeta viviente y apóstoles, usan sus propias escrituras adicionales, edifican templos para ordenanzas sagradas, y son ampliamente conocidos por sus jóvenes misioneros. Mucho en su conducta es admirable. Nuestra preocupación no es su diligencia sino lo que enseñan acerca de Dios, de Cristo y de la salvación.

blocks.en: What They Teach, in Their Own Terms
blocks.es_reference: Lo Que Enseñan, en Sus Propios Términos

blocks.en: Concerning God, the Latter-day Saints reject the Trinity. They teach that the Godhead is three separate beings, each a god, united in purpose; that the Father has a body of flesh and bones; and, most strikingly, that God the Father was once a man who, over long ages, progressed to godhood. Their fifth president summarized it: "As man now is, God once was; as God now is, man may become." They teach, therefore, that many gods exist, and that faithful Latter-day Saints may themselves one day become gods.
blocks.es_reference: En cuanto a Dios, los Santos de los Últimos Días rechazan la Trinidad. Enseñan que la Divinidad son tres seres separados, cada uno un dios, unidos en propósito; que el Padre tiene un cuerpo de carne y huesos; y, lo más sorprendente, que Dios el Padre fue una vez un hombre que, a lo largo de largas edades, progresó hasta la divinidad. Su quinto presidente lo resumió: "Como el hombre es ahora, Dios fue una vez; como Dios es ahora, el hombre puede llegar a ser." Enseñan, por tanto, que existen muchos dioses, y que los Santos fieles pueden ellos mismos un día llegar a ser dioses.

blocks.en: Concerning our origin, they teach that all people lived first as spirit children of Heavenly Father (and a Heavenly Mother). Jesus, they say, was the firstborn of these spirit children, and so the elder spirit brother of all humanity — and of Lucifer as well, since Satan too is held to be a spirit son of God who rebelled. Jesus then became a god before His mortal birth.
blocks.es_reference: En cuanto a nuestro origen, enseñan que todas las personas vivieron primero como hijos espirituales del Padre Celestial (y de una Madre Celestial). Jesús, dicen, fue el primogénito de estos hijos espirituales, y por tanto el hermano espiritual mayor de toda la humanidad — y también de Lucifer, pues se sostiene que Satanás también es un hijo espiritual de Dios que se rebeló. Jesús entonces llegó a ser un dios antes de su nacimiento mortal.

blocks.en: Concerning Jesus, they honor Him as Savior, affirm His atoning death and His bodily resurrection, and call Him the Son of God. Yet within their system He is one of several gods, a being who Himself progressed to godhood, the eldest of the Father's spirit children — not the one eternal God the Son.
blocks.es_reference: En cuanto a Jesús, lo honran como Salvador, afirman su muerte expiatoria y su resurrección corporal, y lo llaman el Hijo de Dios. Sin embargo, dentro de su sistema Él es uno de varios dioses, un ser que Él mismo progresó hasta la divinidad, el mayor de los hijos espirituales del Padre — no el único Dios el Hijo eterno.

blocks.en: Concerning authority, they accept the Bible "as far as it is translated correctly," and add to it the Book of Mormon, the Doctrine and Covenants, and the Pearl of Great Price, along with continuing revelation through a living prophet.
blocks.es_reference: En cuanto a la autoridad, aceptan la Biblia "hasta donde esté traducida correctamente", y le añaden el Libro de Mormón, Doctrina y Convenios, y la Perla de Gran Precio, junto con la revelación continua por medio de un profeta viviente.

blocks.en: Concerning salvation, they teach that nearly all people are "saved" by grace into one of three kingdoms of glory through the universal resurrection. But the highest, called exaltation or eternal life — godhood in the celestial kingdom — must be obtained by accepting the restored gospel, repentance, baptism by their priesthood, temple ordinances, tithing, and obedience to the commandments. Their own scripture says we are saved by grace "after all we can do." We have stated these things as fairly as we can. Now we must test them by Scripture.
blocks.es_reference: En cuanto a la salvación, enseñan que casi todas las personas son "salvas" por gracia a uno de tres reinos de gloria mediante la resurrección universal. Pero el más alto, llamado exaltación o vida eterna — la divinidad en el reino celestial — debe obtenerse aceptando el evangelio restaurado, el arrepentimiento, el bautismo por su sacerdocio, las ordenanzas del templo, el diezmo, y la obediencia a los mandamientos. Su propia escritura dice que somos salvos por gracia "después de todo lo que podamos hacer." Hemos expuesto estas cosas tan justamente como podemos. Ahora debemos probarlas por la Escritura.

blocks.en: Testing the Root (1): A Different God and a Different Christ
blocks.es_reference: Probando la Raíz (1): Un Dios Diferente y un Cristo Diferente

blocks.en: Once again everything turns on the root. Scripture knows nothing of many gods or of a God who was once a man. The LORD declares, "Before Me there was no God formed, nor shall there be after Me" (Isaiah 43:10); "I am the First and I am the Last; besides Me there is no God" (Isaiah 44:6); "Is there a God besides Me? Indeed there is no other Rock; I know not one" (Isaiah 44:8). He is "from everlasting to everlasting" God (Psalm 90:2), and He says, "I am the LORD, I do not change" (Malachi 3:6). A God who was once a man and progressed to godhood, and creatures who become gods, are not in the Bible; there is one eternal, unchanging God, and the line between the Creator and the creature can never be crossed. And the true Christ is not a created spirit brother of Lucifer but the eternal Word, "the Word was God" (John 1:1), through whom "all things were made" (John 1:3) — "all things... whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers" (Colossians 1:16), which means the angelic powers, Lucifer among them, are His creatures, not His brothers. The angels worship Him (Hebrews 1:6). The God and the Christ of the Latter-day Saints are not the God and the Christ of the Scriptures.
blocks.es_reference: Una vez más todo gira en torno a la raíz. La Escritura no sabe nada de muchos dioses ni de un Dios que fue una vez un hombre. Jehová declara: "Antes de mí no fue formado dios, ni lo será después de mí" (Isaías 43:10); "Yo soy el primero, y yo soy el postrero, y fuera de mí no hay Dios" (Isaías 44:6); "¿Hay Dios fuera de mí? No hay Roca; no conozco ninguna" (Isaías 44:8). Él es Dios "desde el siglo y hasta el siglo" (Salmo 90:2), y dice: "yo Jehová no cambio" (Malaquías 3:6). Un Dios que fue una vez hombre y progresó hasta la divinidad, y criaturas que llegan a ser dioses, no están en la Biblia; hay un solo Dios eterno e inmutable, y la línea entre el Creador y la criatura nunca puede cruzarse. Y el verdadero Cristo no es un hermano espiritual creado de Lucifer sino el Verbo eterno, "el Verbo era Dios" (Juan 1:1), por quien "todas las cosas fueron hechas" (Juan 1:3) — "todas las cosas... sean tronos, sean dominios, sean principados, sean potestades" (Colosenses 1:16), lo que significa que las potestades angélicas, Lucifer entre ellas, son sus criaturas, no sus hermanos. Los ángeles le adoran (Hebreos 1:6). El Dios y el Cristo de los Santos de los Últimos Días no son el Dios y el Cristo de las Escrituras.

blocks.en: Testing the Root (2): A Different Gospel of Salvation
blocks.es_reference: Probando la Raíz (2): Un Evangelio de Salvación Diferente

blocks.en: The second failure is the one Galatians was written to answer. To gain exaltation the Latter-day Saint must add to Christ a long list of works — baptism by their priesthood, temple ordinances, tithing, and lifelong obedience — and even their grace is "grace after all we can do." But Paul says, "a man is not justified by the works of the law but by faith in Jesus Christ" (Galatians 2:16); "I do not set aside the grace of God; for if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died in vain" (Galatians 2:21). Salvation is "by grace... through faith... not of works, lest anyone should boast" (Ephesians 2:8-9); it is "not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to His mercy" (Titus 3:5); and "if by grace, then it is no longer of works" (Romans 11:6). Eternal life is not a prize earned by ordinances but "the gift of God... in Christ Jesus our Lord" (Romans 6:23), and it is a present and certain possession: the believer "has passed from death into life" (John 5:24) and may "know that you have eternal life" (1 John 5:13). Nor is salvation channeled through one church's priesthood, "for there is one God and one Mediator between God and men, the Man Christ Jesus" (1 Timothy 2:5). To make exaltation rest on works and ordinances is to change the root.
blocks.es_reference: El segundo fallo es aquel que Gálatas fue escrita para responder. Para alcanzar la exaltación el Santo de los Últimos Días debe añadir a Cristo una larga lista de obras — el bautismo por su sacerdocio, las ordenanzas del templo, el diezmo, y la obediencia de toda la vida — y aun su gracia es "gracia después de todo lo que podamos hacer." Pero Pablo dice: "el hombre no es justificado por las obras de la ley, sino por la fe de Jesucristo" (Gálatas 2:16); "No desecho la gracia de Dios; pues si por la ley fuese la justicia, entonces por demás murió Cristo" (Gálatas 2:21). La salvación es "por gracia... por medio de la fe... no por obras, para que nadie se gloríe" (Efesios 2:8-9); es "no por obras de justicia que nosotros hubiéramos hecho, sino por su misericordia" (Tito 3:5); y "si por gracia, ya no es por obras" (Romanos 11:6). La vida eterna no es un premio ganado por ordenanzas sino "la dádiva de Dios... en Cristo Jesús Señor nuestro" (Romanos 6:23), y es una posesión presente y segura: el creyente "ha pasado de muerte a vida" (Juan 5:24) y puede "saber que tiene vida eterna" (1 Juan 5:13). Ni se canaliza la salvación por el sacerdocio de una iglesia, "porque hay un solo Dios, y un solo mediador entre Dios y los hombres, Jesucristo hombre" (1 Timoteo 2:5). Hacer que la exaltación descanse sobre obras y ordenanzas es cambiar la raíz.

blocks.en: Why This Is "Another Gospel"
blocks.es_reference: Por Qué Esto Es "Otro Evangelio"

blocks.en: A message that gives us many gods, a Christ who is a created spirit brother of Lucifer, and an exaltation earned by ordinances is not the same gospel with extra features; it is "a different gospel, which is not another" (Galatians 1:6-7). Paul's warning is solemn, and it touches the very origin of this movement: "even if we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel to you than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed" (Galatians 1:8). Latter-day Saints trace their gospel to the visit of an angel; but Paul says that no angel, and no human prophet, however sincere, may bring a gospel other than the one already given. For the true gospel is "the faith which was once for all delivered to the saints" (Jude 3); it did not need to be re-revealed in the nineteenth century. The issue is not the morality or sincerity of the Latter-day Saints, in which they are exemplary. The issue is whether there is one eternal God, whether Jesus is that God the Son, and whether sinners are saved by grace. On all three, this is another gospel.
blocks.es_reference: Un mensaje que nos da muchos dioses, un Cristo que es un hermano espiritual creado de Lucifer, y una exaltación ganada por ordenanzas no es el mismo evangelio con rasgos adicionales; es "otro evangelio; no que haya otro" (Gálatas 1:6-7). La advertencia de Pablo es solemne, y toca el origen mismo de este movimiento: "si aun nosotros, o un ángel del cielo os predicare otro evangelio diferente del que os hemos predicado, sea anatema" (Gálatas 1:8). Los Santos de los Últimos Días sitúan su evangelio en la visita de un ángel; pero Pablo dice que ningún ángel, y ningún profeta humano, por sincero que sea, puede traer un evangelio distinto del ya dado. Pues el verdadero evangelio es "la fe que ha sido una vez dada a los santos" (Judas 3); no necesitaba ser revelado de nuevo en el siglo diecinueve. La cuestión no es la moralidad ni la sinceridad de los Santos de los Últimos Días, en lo cual son ejemplares. La cuestión es si hay un solo Dios eterno, si Jesús es ese Dios el Hijo, y si los pecadores son salvos por gracia. En las tres, este es otro evangelio.

blocks.en: The Book of Mormon and DNA
blocks.es_reference: El Libro de Mormón y el ADN

blocks.en: The Latter-day Saint faith rests not only on distinctive doctrines but on a book that presents itself as real history. The Book of Mormon tells of ancient peoples in the Americas, chiefly a family led by the prophet Lehi said to have sailed from Jerusalem about 600 B.C.; their descendants, the Nephites and Lamanites, are portrayed as principal ancestors of the American Indians — indeed the book's own introduction long described the Lamanites as "the principal ancestors of the American Indians" (softened in 2006 to "among the ancestors"). This is a testable historical claim, and modern population genetics has tested it. Extensive study of the DNA of native peoples across North, Central, and South America — both the mitochondrial line and the Y-chromosome — consistently traces their ancestry to eastern Asia and Siberia by way of migration across the Bering region, and finds no distinctive Near-Eastern or Israelite genetic signature among pre-Columbian populations. In fairness, the Church has answered this in an official essay, Book of Mormon and DNA Studies. It argues that the record never claims Lehi's family were the only people in the Americas; that on a "limited geography" reading the events may have occupied a small region, so that a tiny founding group's DNA could have been absorbed and rendered undetectable within far larger surrounding populations; and that genetics therefore cannot finally prove or disprove the account. Others reply that for more than a century the book and its teachers presented these peoples as the principal ancestors of the American Indians, and that the limited-geography defense is itself a significant retreat from that long-held claim; writers within the Latter-day Saint intellectual tradition, in journals such as Dialogue: A Journal of Mormon Thought, have argued that the genetic evidence is fundamentally inconsistent with the traditional narrative. The believer need not settle every technical dispute to see the point: the historical foundation on which this second scripture rests is, at the least, gravely in question — and behind the question of the book stands the deeper question of the gospel it teaches.
blocks.es_reference: La fe de los Santos de los Últimos Días descansa no solo en doctrinas distintivas sino en un libro que se presenta como historia real. El Libro de Mormón narra pueblos antiguos en las Américas, principalmente una familia guiada por el profeta Lehi que, se dice, navegó desde Jerusalén alrededor del año 600 a.C.; sus descendientes, los nefitas y los lamanitas, son presentados como principales antepasados de los indios americanos — de hecho la propia introducción del libro describió por mucho tiempo a los lamanitas como "los principales antepasados de los indios americanos" (suavizado en 2006 a "entre los antepasados"). Esta es una afirmación histórica comprobable, y la genética de poblaciones moderna la ha comprobado. El estudio extenso del ADN de los pueblos nativos de América del Norte, Central y del Sur — tanto la línea mitocondrial como el cromosoma Y — traza consistentemente su ascendencia al este de Asia y a Siberia por medio de la migración a través de la región de Bering, y no halla ninguna firma genética distintiva del Cercano Oriente ni de Israel entre las poblaciones precolombinas. En justicia, la Iglesia ha respondido a esto en un ensayo oficial, El Libro de Mormón y los Estudios de ADN. Argumenta que el registro nunca afirma que la familia de Lehi fuera el único pueblo en las Américas; que en una lectura de "geografía limitada" los sucesos pudieron ocupar una región pequeña, de modo que el ADN de un grupo fundador diminuto pudo haber sido absorbido y quedar indetectable dentro de poblaciones circundantes mucho mayores; y que la genética, por tanto, no puede finalmente probar ni refutar el relato. Otros responden que por más de un siglo el libro y sus maestros presentaron a estos pueblos como los principales antepasados de los indios americanos, y que la defensa de la geografía limitada es en sí misma un retroceso significativo de esa afirmación sostenida por tanto tiempo; escritores dentro de la tradición intelectual de los Santos de los Últimos Días, en revistas como Dialogue: A Journal of Mormon Thought, han argumentado que la evidencia genética es fundamentalmente incompatible con la narrativa tradicional. El creyente no necesita resolver cada disputa técnica para ver el punto: el fundamento histórico sobre el cual descansa esta segunda escritura está, por lo menos, gravemente en cuestión — y detrás de la cuestión del libro está la cuestión más profunda del evangelio que enseña.

blocks.en: The Question of Fellowship
blocks.es_reference: La Cuestión de la Comunión

blocks.en: This leads to the same hard but necessary conclusion. Because the Latter-day Saints confess a different God, a different Christ, and a different gospel, we cannot recognize their teaching as the Christian faith, nor join with it in the fellowship and work of the gospel. This is not personal hostility and never a license for unkindness. We honor them as neighbors, treat them with courtesy and warmth, and gladly do them good. But love does not pretend. Scripture will not let us call a different God and a different gospel merely another Christian tradition: "Whoever transgresses and does not abide in the doctrine of Christ does not have God... If anyone comes to you and does not bring this doctrine, do not receive him into your house nor greet him" (2 John 9-10) — that is, do not welcome him as a fellow worker or endorse his message. We are not to be "unequally yoked together with unbelievers" (2 Corinthians 6:14). So we do not share in their worship or their mission, for it rests upon another foundation; yet we gladly reason with them from the Scriptures.
blocks.es_reference: Esto lleva a la misma conclusión difícil pero necesaria. Porque los Santos de los Últimos Días confiesan un Dios diferente, un Cristo diferente, y un evangelio diferente, no podemos reconocer su enseñanza como la fe cristiana, ni unirnos con ella en la comunión y la obra del evangelio. Esto no es hostilidad personal y nunca licencia para la descortesía. Los honramos como prójimos, los tratamos con cortesía y calidez, y con gusto les hacemos bien. Pero el amor no finge. La Escritura no nos deja llamar a un Dios diferente y un evangelio diferente meramente otra tradición cristiana: "Cualquiera que se rebela, y no persevera en la doctrina de Cristo, no tiene a Dios... Si alguno viene a vosotros, y no trae esta doctrina, no lo recibáis en casa, ni le digáis: ¡Bienvenido!" (2 Juan 9-10) — es decir, no lo recibáis como colaborador ni aprobéis su mensaje. No hemos de unirnos "en yugo desigual con los incrédulos" (2 Corintios 6:14). Así que no participamos de su culto ni de su misión, pues descansa sobre otro fundamento; pero con gusto razonamos con ellos desde las Escrituras.

blocks.en: A Redemptive Aim
blocks.es_reference: Un Fin Redentor

blocks.en: And all of this is for a redemptive end. We draw these lines not to shut people out but because we long for the Latter-day Saints to come in — to the true God and the true Christ. The good news we bring them is greater than the gospel they have received: there are not many gods but one, eternal and unchanging, who was never a man and who shares His glory with no other; and Jesus is not a god who progressed but the eternal Son, the Creator come in the flesh, who gives full, free, and certain salvation to all who trust Him — with no ordinance to complete it and no doubt to cloud it. Many Latter-day Saints sincerely seek God and live upright lives; we pray that God will lead them to rest in the finished work of the one Lord Jesus Christ. We treat each one as a person Christ died to save — with patience, prayer, and an open Bible.
blocks.es_reference: Y todo esto es para un fin redentor. Trazamos estas líneas no para dejar a la gente afuera sino porque anhelamos que los Santos de los Últimos Días entren — al verdadero Dios y al verdadero Cristo. Las buenas nuevas que les traemos son mayores que el evangelio que han recibido: no hay muchos dioses sino uno, eterno e inmutable, que nunca fue un hombre y que no comparte su gloria con ningún otro; y Jesús no es un dios que progresó sino el Hijo eterno, el Creador venido en carne, que da salvación plena, gratuita y segura a todo el que confía en Él — sin ordenanza que la complete y sin duda que la nuble. Muchos Santos de los Últimos Días buscan sinceramente a Dios y viven vidas rectas; oramos que Dios los lleve a descansar en la obra consumada del único Señor Jesucristo. Tratamos a cada uno como una persona por quien Cristo murió para salvar — con paciencia, oración, y la Biblia abierta.

mc.stem: The Latter-day Saints teach that the Godhead is:
options: Three separate Gods, united in purpose
mc.why: They reject the Trinity and hold the Godhead to be separate gods.

mc.stem: The Latter-day Saints teach that God the Father:
options: has a body of flesh and bones
is the same person as the Son
mc.why: They teach the Father has a tangible body of flesh and bones.

mc.stem: The Lorenzo Snow couplet says, 'As man now is, God once was; as God now is, ___.'
mc.why: It teaches that God was once a man and man may become a god.

mc.stem: The Latter-day Saints teach that faithful humans may ultimately:
mc.why: Exaltation is the goal: godhood in the celestial kingdom.

mc.stem: The Latter-day Saints teach that, before His mortal birth, Jesus was:
options: the firstborn spirit child of Heavenly Father
mc.why: They teach Jesus was the firstborn of God's spirit children.

mc.stem: The Latter-day Saints teach that Jesus and Lucifer are:
options: enemies from eternity past who were never related
spirit brothers (both spirit children of God)
mc.why: In their teaching, Satan too is a spirit son of God, Jesus' brother.

mc.stem: Besides the Bible, Latter-day Saint scriptures include:
options: only the writings of the apostles
the Book of Mormon, Doctrine and Covenants, and Pearl of Great Price
mc.why: They add three further books of scripture to the Bible.

mc.stem: The Book of Mormon presents Lehi's family (from Jerusalem) as principal ancestors of the American Indians. Modern DNA studies of Native peoples show their ancestry is:
options: an equal mix of Hebrew and Asian
overwhelmingly East Asian and Siberian, with no distinctive Israelite signature
mc.why: Population genetics traces Native American ancestry to eastern Asia and Siberia, finding no distinctive Near-Eastern or Israelite genetic signature.

mc.stem: For the highest salvation (exaltation), Latter-day Saints teach one must:
options: receive priesthood ordinances, pay tithing, and obey
mc.why: Exaltation requires ordinances, tithing, and obedience added to faith.

mc.stem: In its official essay Book of Mormon and DNA Studies, the Church responds that:
options: the DNA evidence positively proves the Book of Mormon
the Book of Mormon is merely a parable, not history
DNA science is a deliberate fraud
the record need not describe the only inhabitants, so a small group's DNA could be undetectable within larger populations (a 'limited geography' view)
mc.why: The essay argues the Book of Mormon does not claim its peoples were the only inhabitants, and on a limited-geography reading a small founding group's DNA could be undetectable — so genetics cannot finally settle the account.

mc.stem: Scripture teaches that there is:
options: only one God, eternal and unchanging
one God who was once a man
mc.why: There is one eternal God who never was a man (Isaiah 44:6; Malachi 3:6).

mc.stem: Isaiah 44:6 says, 'I am the First and I am the Last; besides Me there is ___.'
mc.why: God knows of no other God beside Himself.

mc.stem: John 1:3 and Colossians 1:16 teach that Jesus:
options: created all things, including the angelic powers
mc.why: The Creator of all things, including Lucifer, cannot be Lucifer's brother.

mc.stem: Malachi 3:6 says, 'I am the LORD, ___.'
mc.why: God does not change; He was never a man who progressed.

mc.stem: According to Romans 6:23, eternal life is:
options: the gift of God in Christ Jesus
mc.why: Eternal life is a free gift, not a prize earned by works.

mc.stem: John 5:24 and 1 John 5:13 teach that the believer:
options: already has eternal life and may know it
mc.why: Salvation is a present possession with assurance, not uncertainty.

mc.stem: According to 1 Timothy 2:5, salvation is mediated by:
options: the one Mediator, the Man Christ Jesus
mc.why: Christ alone mediates salvation, not a church or its priesthood.

mc.stem: 'The faith once for all delivered to the saints' (Jude 3) means the gospel:
options: did not need a new restoration
mc.why: The gospel was delivered once for all; it needed no 19th-century restoration.

mc.stem: Because they confess a different God, Christ, and gospel, the unit concludes we:
options: cannot share gospel fellowship with their teaching
mc.why: We cannot treat a different gospel as the same faith, yet we are never cruel.

mc.stem: The unit's posture toward Latter-day Saints as people is:
options: redemptive love that points them to the true God and Christ
mc.why: We love them, treat them kindly, and long for them to know the true Christ.

sa.prompt: Fairly summarize what the Latter-day Saints teach about God.
sa.model: The Latter-day Saints reject the Trinity. They teach that the Godhead is three separate beings, each a god, united in purpose, and that the Father has a body of flesh and bones while the Holy Ghost is a personage of spirit. Most strikingly, they teach that God the Father was once a man who progressed over long ages to godhood, summarized in the couplet, as man now is, God once was; as God now is, man may become. They therefore hold that many gods exist, and that faithful Latter-day Saints may themselves attain exaltation and become gods. So their doctrine of God denies both the Trinity and the unique, eternal, unchanging nature of the one true God.

sa.prompt: Fairly summarize what the Latter-day Saints teach about Jesus.
sa.model: The Latter-day Saints teach that Jesus was the firstborn spirit child of Heavenly Father in a pre-mortal existence, and therefore the elder spirit brother of all humans. They also teach that Lucifer is a spirit son of God, which makes Jesus and Lucifer spirit brothers. Jesus, they say, became a god before His mortal birth. They honor Him as Savior, affirm His atoning death and bodily resurrection, and call Him the Son of God. Yet within their system He is one of several gods, a created spirit who Himself progressed, rather than the one eternal God the Son. So their Jesus, though called Savior, is a different Christ from the eternal Word of Scripture.

sa.prompt: Fairly summarize what the Latter-day Saints teach about salvation.
sa.model: The Latter-day Saints teach that nearly all people are saved by grace into one of three kingdoms of glory through the universal resurrection. But the highest salvation, called exaltation or eternal life, which is godhood in the celestial kingdom, must be obtained by accepting the restored gospel, repentance, baptism by their priesthood, temple ordinances, tithing, and obedience to the commandments. Their own scripture says we are saved by grace after all we can do, so works are essential to the highest salvation. In short, they add ordinances and works to grace, and tie exaltation to their church, denying that salvation is by grace through faith alone.

sa.prompt: From Scripture, show that there is only one God, eternal and unchanging.
sa.model: Scripture teaches that there is only one God, eternal and unchanging, not many gods and not a God who was once a man. The LORD says that before Him no God was formed, nor shall there be after Him, and that He is the First and the Last, with no God besides Him; indeed He knows of no other. He is God from everlasting to everlasting, the Creator of all, and He says plainly, I do not change. Because God does not change and was never formed, the idea that He was once a man who progressed, or that creatures become gods, cannot be true. There is one eternal God, and the line between the Creator and the creature is never crossed.

sa.prompt: From Scripture, show that Jesus is the eternal Creator, not a created spirit brother of Lucifer.
sa.model: Scripture teaches that Jesus is the eternal Creator, not a created being. John says the Word was God and that all things were made through Him, and Paul says that by Christ all things were created, whether thrones or dominions or powers. Since Christ created all things, including the angelic powers, Lucifer is His creature and not His brother. The eternal Word cannot be one of the spirit children who were created. Furthermore, the angels worship Christ, which an angel or a fellow creature could never receive. So Jesus is the eternal God the Son, the Creator of Lucifer and of all things, and to call Him Lucifer's spirit brother denies His true deity.

sa.prompt: From Scripture, show that salvation is a free gift by grace and is assured, not exaltation earned by ordinances.
sa.model: Scripture teaches that salvation is by grace through faith, a free gift, not earned by works or ordinances. Paul says we are saved by grace through faith, and not of ourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, and if it is by grace it is no longer of works. Eternal life is the gift of God in Christ Jesus, not a prize earned by temple ordinances and tithing. And this salvation is assured: the one who believes has passed from death into life, and these things are written so that believers may have assurance and know they have eternal life. To add ordinances and works to grace, and to deny present assurance, contradicts the grace of God and changes the gospel.

sa.prompt: Explain why Latter-day Saint teaching is 'another gospel' (Galatians 1:6-9), and the force of 'even an angel.'
sa.model: Latter-day Saint teaching is another gospel because it changes the root at three points: it gives many gods instead of one eternal God, a Christ who is a created spirit brother of Lucifer instead of the eternal Son, and an exaltation earned by ordinances instead of salvation by grace. Paul says such a message is a different gospel, not really another, and his warning is severe: even if an angel from heaven preaches another gospel, let him be accursed. This lands with force because the movement traces its restored gospel to the visit of an angel; yet no angel and no human prophet may bring a gospel other than the one already delivered. The faith was once for all delivered to the saints, so it needed no new restoration, and to change the root is to fall under Paul's warning.

sa.prompt: Explain the unit's conclusion about fellowship, and how to hold it with charity.
sa.model: The unit concludes that because the Latter-day Saints confess a different God, Christ, and gospel, we cannot recognize their teaching as the Christian faith or join with it in gospel fellowship. John says that whoever does not abide in the doctrine of Christ does not have God, and that we should not receive such a one or endorse his message as a fellow worker. Yet this must be held with charity and kindness. We love each person, treat them with courtesy and warmth, and gladly do them good. We refuse fellowship with the false teaching, not friendship with the people. We may reason with them from Scripture; we simply may not stand beside them as heralds of the same gospel or lend approval to a teaching that denies the one true God and the eternal Christ.

sa.prompt: Summarize the challenge that population genetics poses to the Book of Mormon's account of American origins, and fairly state how the Church responds in its Book of Mormon and DNA Studies essay.
sa.model: The Book of Mormon presents Lehi's family, who sailed from Jerusalem, as principal ancestors of the American Indians. Modern population genetics challenges this: extensive study of the DNA of Native peoples — both mitochondrial and Y-chromosome lines — traces their ancestry overwhelmingly to eastern Asia and Siberia, and finds no distinctive Israelite or Near-Eastern signature in pre-Columbian populations. In fairness, the Church answers in its essay Book of Mormon and DNA Studies that the record never claims Lehi's family were the only inhabitants; that on a limited geography reading the events occupied a small region, so a tiny founding group's DNA could have been absorbed and undetectable within far larger surrounding populations; and that DNA therefore cannot finally prove or disprove the account. Critics reply that this is a significant retreat from the long-held claim that these peoples were the principal ancestors of Native Americans. Either way, the historical foundation of this second scripture is gravely in question.

sa.prompt: Summarize Unit 4: the Latter-day Saint gospel tested by the root, the verdict, and the redemptive aim.
sa.model: Unit 4 tests the gospel of the Latter-day Saints by the root and reaches a clear verdict. At the root they place many gods and a God who was once a man, a Christ who is a created spirit brother of Lucifer, and an exaltation earned by ordinances and works rather than salvation by grace. Because they change the root in the doctrine of God, the person of Christ, and the way of salvation, theirs is another gospel under Paul's warning, and we cannot share gospel fellowship with their teaching. Yet the aim is redemptive, not hostile. We love the Latter-day Saints as people, treat them with kindness, and long for them to come to the one eternal God and the true Christ, who gives full and free salvation by grace through faith. We hold the true gospel firmly and reach out to them in love.
